messages:
eliza (Customer): Hey — got our monthly invoice and tokens billed are ~1.2M but the Usage dashboard shows ~820k. Can someone explain why the invoice is so much higher?

cora (Support): Sorry about that, @eliza. Can you share an example request_id or a couple of timestamps so we can correlate? Is this for the hosted API or a Dedicated pool?

eliza (Customer): Hosted API. Example request_id: req_01F8Y2Z5, seen around 2025-12-05T14:12Z. We observed spikes on Dec 4–6. Most calls are short completions (~25 tokens).

cora (Support): Thanks. One quick check — do you use streaming or the chat endpoint with function-calling? Also any prefix/KV cache enabled?

eliza (Customer): Chat endpoint, no functions. We enabled prefix caching (kv cache) to avoid re-sending a 60-token system prompt on every request.

james (SRE): @cora tagging runtime infra. Common cause: continuous batching + padding can inflate billed tokens if billing pipeline counts before de-dup/caching. Can you paste a sample curl that reproduces?

eliza (Customer): Sure — reproducible with this script hitting the chat endpoint concurrently:

```bash
for i in {1..40}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-large-2025","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"[TEN-SECOND PROMPT-60TOK]"},{"role":"user","content":"short ask"}]}' &\
done
wait
```

We then inspected response headers and sometimes see `X-Redwood-Served-Tokens: 480` and `X-Redwood-Metered-Tokens: 120` for the same request_id, but the totals on invoice look closer to summing the Served values across all requests.

repro-bot: automated note — thread contains request_id req_01F8Y2Z5 and sample script.

leo (Runtime): Interesting. The runtime currently applies continuous batching that pads sequences in a batch to the max length. Served tokens header reports tokens touched by the runtime (post-padding). Metered tokens header reports tokens attributed to billing pipeline (we intended post-cache, but there is a race). Ideally metered <= served when cache hits reduce work, but our pipeline bug sometimes double-counts pad tokens before cache dedupe.

marta (Billing): To confirm: our invoicing job uses the billing stream which currently reads the raw token count emitted by the front-end ingress (pre-cache dedupe). That would explain higher invoice totals if the ingress counted padded batch tokens. We're supposed to use the deduped metered stream.

cora (Support): So this matches the pattern: many short requests + prefix cache + continuous batching -> lots of padding to match longest in batch -> ingress counts padded tokens -> billing job pulls ingress count -> invoice inflated. Meanwhile the Usage dashboard consumes the post-cache deduped stream and shows lower numbers.

eliza (Customer): That lines up with what we saw. Is there a workaround we can apply on our side right now? We're very sensitive to token cost.

james (SRE): Short-term mitigation: disable continuous batching for your key or reduce concurrency to avoid large padding. We can also whitelist your account to use the post-dedupe metered stream while we fix the pipeline.

leo (Runtime): Repro steps for us (internal): 1) Run the attached concurrency script against rw-large-2025 with prefix cache enabled. 2) Watch runtime logs for batch formation and padded lengths: `DEBUG runtime.batch: batch_size=24 max_seq=64 pad_total=960`. 3) Compare headers: `X-Redwood-Ingress-Pad-Tokens`, `X-Redwood-Served-Tokens`, `X-Redwood-Metered-Tokens`.

cora (Support): @marta can you confirm whether we can re-run invoicing for Dec 4–6 for eliza's org using the post-dedupe stream? If yes we can issue an adjustment.

marta (Billing): I can run an audit. Please provide the org id and invoice id. If root cause confirmed (ingress pre-dedupe counts used), we'll credit the delta. Pls send privately.

eliza (Customer): Sent org id + invoice id in DM. Also — can you add a response header that makes the difference explicit for us? Like `X-Redwood-Billed-Tokens` vs `X-Redwood-Served-Tokens`?

leo (Runtime): Good idea. Quick patch: expose `X-Redwood-Runtime-Padded-Tokens` and `X-Redwood-Cache-Hit` boolean for a trial. I'll push a canary to hosted API tomorrow and capture a sample.

james (SRE): Action items: 1) @leo deploy canary header (ETA: 24h). 2) @marta run audit for invoices (ETA: 48h). 3) @cora offer eliza temporary whitelist to post-dedupe billing stream + disable continuous batching for eliza's key if needed. 4) engineering follow-up to fix billing pipeline to use post-dedupe counts (longer term).

cora (Support): @eliza we'll follow up asynchronously and keep you updated. Sorry for the friction — appreciate the repro script, that sped this up a lot. :heart:
